meeting_header:
Date: 2025-06-04 | Time: 15:00-15:57 UTC | Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Ava Mitchell (Redwood AE), Ravi Shah (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (Cobalt Head of Procurement), Ethan Park (Cobalt Legal), Lina Gomez (Cloud Infra), Noah Reed (CISO)
summary: Procurement + legal intake to validate MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs, pricing approval path and technical requirements for private deployment options. Customer needs: encryption BYOK, data residency in EU for certain datasets, explicit audit logs and SOC2 evidence. Redwood to provide redlines, security packet, and run benchmarks for cost/latency delta between hosted and dedicated/reserved offerings.
topics: MSA redlines: indemnity and liability caps
DPA specifics: data localization and subprocessors
Pricing approvals: committed discounts, overage billing, egress fees
Security: SOC2, penetration tests, KMS/BYOK, SSO/SAML
Deployment options: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
transcript:
00:00:00 - Ava: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we're hoping to run through the contractual questions and then jump into the technical asks, we've got about 55 minutes, is that still good?
00:00:10 - Dana: Yep that works, Dana here, head of procurement for Cobalt, thanks Ava.
00:00:15 - Ethan: Ethan on legal, I'll be driving the redline review.
00:00:18 - Lina: Lina, infra. I'll focus on the network/KMS bits.
00:00:21 - Noah: Noah, CISO, short intro from me on controls.
00:00:27 - Ravi: Ravi from Redwood, SE, I'll cover benchmarks and technical constraints.
00:00:33 - Ava: Great, quick agenda: MSA/DPA high level, SLA and penalties, pricing/commits, then technical clarifications around KMS and VPC. We'll capture next steps.
00:01:05 - Dana: On MSA, main ask from procurement is liability cap alignment and exit rights in case of data incidents. Last vendor wanted a 12 month notice exit which is too long for our procurement runway.
00:01:22 - Ethan: Also interested in subprocessors list in the DPA, we need explicit disclosure of any third-party infra providers and where data moves.
00:01:35 - Ava: Understood. On liability cap, our standard is 2x annual spend or $5M - we can present options. For data incidents, we can add an expedited termination clause tied to material breach. Would that be acceptable?
00:01:55 - Ethan: That's reasonable as a starting point. Need to see exact language.
00:02:10 - Lina: For the subprocessors - we have a firm requirement for EU residency on PHI-adjacent logs; if any tokenization or PHI-adjacent data leaves region that's problematic. Can Redwood support region pinning for those workloads?
00:02:30 - Ravi: Yes, we support regional routing. For hosted we have EU regions that can be pinned per request or per customer. For Dedicated or Private deployments you can keep everything in your VPC. There's a nuance with model variants and fallback — if a region is saturated we can route to a compatible variant but only with consent or an allow-list.
00:02:52 - Noah: We want the fallback behavior explicit in the SLA — no silent cross-region fallback without notice.
00:03:01 - Ava: Noted. We'll include a clause: any automatic cross-region fallback requires an advance notification and toggle in console.
00:03:10 - Dana: Pricing — procurement needs to understand commit levels. We're looking at a 12-month reserved capacity for predictable costs, but we need an internal cost model to present to finance.
00:03:23 - Ravi: We'll run a benchmark with your sample prompts and traffic to show token cost, p95 latency, and cost delta between hosted, dedicated, and private. Typical committed discounts range 15-30% depending on spend.
00:03:36 - Lina: Important detail: what about network egress and inter-region transfer fees? Our cloud billers hate surprise egress.
00:03:44 - Ava: Egress is charged per cloud provider egress policy; we can provide estimates and also include a capped egress allowance in the reserved package if needed.
00:03:54 - Ethan: For DPA we want explicit subcontractor list and a right to audit. Is Redwood open to an audit window or a SOC2 certificate plus third-party pen test report?
00:04:07 - Ava: We provide SOC2 Type II reports and recent pen test summary; for enterprise deals we can carve an audit clause with reasonable notice and scope limits.
00:04:17 - Noah: What about KMS - do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) or only Redwood-managed keys?
00:04:24 - Ravi: We support customer-managed keys for Private deployments and Dedicated with HSM integrations via major cloud KMS. For hosted, we offer an encryption at-rest default but BYOK is available for enterprise tenants through a managed integration (there's an implementation lead time).
00:04:40 - Lina: Implementation lead time estimate?
00:04:43 - Ravi: Typically 4-8 weeks depending on HSM and contract. We can provide a more precise plan after we see your KMS provider.
00:04:52 - Dana: On SLA — what are the SLOs? Finance expects uptime guarantees and credits.
00:04:59 - Ava: Our baseline hosted SLA is 99.9% monthly for API availability, with latency SLOs at p95 around 300ms for small models and variable for large model generation. Dedicated has a 99.95% uptime SLA and tailored latency targets. Credits scale with downtime windows; we can surface exact table in the SLA.
00:05:22 - Marcus (automated noise)
00:05:26 - Ethan: We need that SLA table in the contract, and a cap on credits that's not de facto unlimited. Also need to ensure the SLA doesn't conflict with force-majeure clauses.
00:05:39 - Ava: We'll include the SLA table and standard force-majeure carveouts; we can negotiate the credit cap.
00:05:47 - Lina: For technical acceptance, we want a short pilot to validate latency and correctness on our prompts — 2 weeks likely. Can that be done in Hosted or do we need Dedicated?
00:05:58 - Ravi: You can absolutely pilot on hosted with a dedicated test account. If your QA indicates that latency/cost requires Dedicated, we can propose a short-term reserved pool for the pilot. The benchmark plan will show likely outcomes.
00:06:15 - Dana: On billing, how are overages handled after a commit? Is it per-token overage at list price or a blended rate?
00:06:23 - Ava: Overage is typically billed at a pre-negotiated overage rate — we can offer a blended step-down if you hit certain tiers. We'll include a billing example in the pricing appendix.
00:06:36 - Ethan: On indemnity - carveouts for IP claims must be mutual. We can't accept unlimited indemnity for third-party outputs.
00:06:45 - Ava: We'll propose mutual IP indemnities and a liability carve that aligns with industry norms.
00:06:51 - Noah: Monitoring and audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for admin actions and model inference logs (meta only, no prompt text) stored for 90 days in EU region.
00:07:04 - Ravi: We can provide admin audit logs and an option for masked inference logs where raw prompt text is redacted. Retention windows and region can be configured.
00:07:15 - Lina: Can you stream logs to our SIEM or SFTP?
00:07:18 - Ravi: Yes, log forwarding to syslog/S3/SFTP or SIEM connectors is supported in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer scheduled exports and an enterprise connectors package.
00:07:32 - Ava: Quick clarification — when you said PHI-adjacent logs, is that strictly healthcare PHI or blended data?
00:07:40 - Lina: It's mixed. We'll likely tokenise or scrub PII before sending but need guarantees for residency.
00:07:48 - Ethan: Also need language around lawful requests and disclosure notifications.
00:07:51 - Ava: We have a standard process for legal requests; we'll share the process doc with timelines.
00:07:58 - Dana: Procurement needs a clear path for pricing approvals — is there a pricing committee step on Redwood's side?
00:08:05 - Ava: For deals above a threshold there's a pricing ops review; I can route approvals faster if we mark this as priority and provide usage forecasts.
00:08:13 - Dana: We'll provide a 12-month forecast with best/worst case.
00:08:17 - Ravi: For the benchmark, a couple of asks from infra: 1) sample prompt corpus 2) expected concurrency 3) expected average sequence length 4) SLA test traffic window.
00:08:29 - Lina: We'll get that by Monday, include two traffic profiles: bursty user queries and batch embedding jobs.
00:08:37 - Ava: Perfect. On redlines, Ethan, are you ok with an initial commercial redline pass from our side before we exchange formal track-changes?
00:08:47 - Ethan: Yes, commercial first then legal. We'll prioritize data handling, audit, and liability.
00:08:53 - Ravi: One small technical note — prefix caching can drastically reduce token costs for repeated queries, but it implies keeping partial KV cache across requests; if you need strict per-request isolation we can disable caching but cost will be higher.
00:09:10 - Lina: We need isolation for certain regulated flows. Can cache be scoped per-tenant or per-route?
00:09:16 - Ravi: Yes, scoping is supported. We'll document caching policies and how they map to cost.
00:09:24 - Dana: Any concerns from Redwood about contractual exposures around generated content — hallucinations and potential defamation?
00:09:33 - Ava: We typically include a standard 'no guarantee of output' clause and require customers to implement user-level controls; we can discuss language that clarifies responsibilities.
00:09:44 - Ethan: We'll want to narrow the consumer-facing obligations.
00:09:47 - Ava: Understood, can handle in the next legal iteration.
00:09:53 - Noah: From security perspective, we'd like a runbook for incident response timeline and notification SLA — 24-hour initial notification, 72-hour detailed report.
00:10:03 - Ava: We can commit to initial notification within 24 hours for confirmed incidents and provide a post-incident report within 72 hours, subject to investigation windows.
00:10:12 - Lina: For private deployments, are you offering an air-gapped option or just VPC with no outbound?
00:10:18 - Ravi: We offer VPC/no-internet and a deployable appliance for extremely regulated customers; air-gapped on-prem is a separate program with longer lead times.
00:10:28 - Dana: Cost modeling — finance will ask for worst-case monthly spend for our 12-month forecast, can you provide a blended and a worst-case?
00:10:36 - Ravi: We'll include hosted baseline, dedicated reserved, and private full stack worst-case. The bench will have cost per 1k tokens and a sample month calculation.
00:10:45 - Ava: Quick check — any blockers to move forward to an initial pilot and legal review?
00:10:50 - Ethan: Main blocker is the MSA/DPA clause visibility and subprocessors list.
00:10:54 - Lina: For infra, blocker is KMS integration timeline and log forwarding details.
00:10:59 - Ava: We'll action both items immediately.
00:11:05 - Dana: Sounds good, can you also include reseller or subcontractor lists in the security packet?
00:11:11 - Ava: Yes, we'll include subprocessors and major cloud provider information.
00:11:18 - Ravi: On the pilot mechanics — we'll provision a sandbox org, capture latency and cost for your sample prompts, and provide access to Redwood Console metrics for your team.
00:11:29 - Lina: Console access will help with acceptance testing; we'll need RBAC for our testers.
00:11:35 - Ava: We'll preconfigure RBAC roles for tester, admin, and billing.
00:11:41 - Ethan: Is there a standard DPA we can review before the redline?
00:11:46 - Ava: Yes, I'll attach the standard DPA and the SOC2 report in the follow-up.
00:11:52 - Dana: Ok next steps recap?
00:11:55 - Ava: Redwood to send redlined MSA and standard DPA, security packet (SOC2, pen test summary), and benchmark plan. SE to start benchmark when sample prompts arrive. Customer to return prioritized redlines.
00:12:07 - Ethan: We'll aim to get redlines back by 6/13.
00:12:11 - Lina: We'll send traffic samples and logs by 6/9.
00:12:15 - Ava: Great. Anything else?
00:12:18 - Noah: One last thing — data residency proof: if we pin workloads to EU, can you commit to not doing any asynchronous processing in US?
00:12:27 - Ravi: We can commit to regional compute for pinned requests; background analytics/telemetry is an opt-out. We'll detail that in the DPA appendix.
00:12:38 - Dana: Thank you all.
00:12:40 - Ava: Thanks team, I'll follow up with the packet and schedule the technical deep-dive next week.
00:12:45 - (meeting continues with brief Q&A and scheduling logistics, and a short side conversation about internal procurement timelines)
00:56:50 - Ava: Closing, appreciate the time, we'll send materials and pick up with legal next week.
00:56:57 - End of recording.
